title: DSA Quiz
description: Categorized DSA quiz imported from source question bank

questions.question: What is the time complexity of accessing an element in an array by index?
Which data structure follows the Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle?
What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort?
In a Binary Search Tree (BST), where is the minimum element always found?
Which traversal of a BST gives elements in sorted (ascending) order?
What is the space complexity of Merge Sort?
Which data structure is best suited for implementing a breadth-first search (BFS)?
What does the 'amortized O(1)' complexity of dynamic array append mean?
options: Each append always takes constant time
Append is O(1) only for small arrays
The average cost per append over many operations is O(1)

questions.question: What is the height of a complete binary tree with n nodes?
Which algorithm is used internally by most standard library sort implementations (like Timsort)?
options: Hybrid of Merge Sort and Insertion Sort

questions.question: What is the time complexity of searching in a balanced Binary Search Tree?
A hash table has O(1) average search time. What causes worst-case O(n) search?
options: All keys hashing to the same bucket (collision)
Using a poor hash function that maps all to index 0

questions.question: What is the key invariant maintained by a Max-Heap?
options: Left child > right child for every node
Every node is greater than or equal to its children
Parent is smaller than both children

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm has the best performance on nearly-sorted data?
What is the time complexity of Dijkstra's algorithm using a binary min-heap?
What property distinguishes a graph tree from a general graph?
options: A tree has no isolated vertices
A tree is a connected acyclic graph
A tree has exactly one cycle

questions.question: What does a topological sort produce for a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)?
options: A linear ordering where every edge goes from earlier to later
The shortest path between all pairs

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?
Which data structure allows O(1) insertion and deletion at both ends?
In dynamic programming, what is 'memoization'?
options: Storing results of expensive subproblems to avoid recomputation
Breaking a problem into independent subproblems
Using recursion without a base case

questions.question: What is the time complexity of the Floyd-Warshall algorithm for finding all-pairs shortest paths?
What is a 'sentinel node' commonly used for in linked list implementations?
options: To mark the end of the list with a null pointer
To simplify edge cases by acting as a dummy head or tail
To track the current traversal position

questions.question: Which graph representation is more space-efficient for sparse graphs?
What is the recurrence relation for Merge Sort's time complexity?
What is the primary advantage of a skip list over a balanced BST?
options: Simpler implementation with similar average-case performance

questions.question: In the Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union) structure, what does 'path compression' do?
options: Finds the shortest path between two nodes
Flattens the tree by pointing nodes directly to the root after a find
Merges two sets using rank heuristic
Removes duplicate elements from a set

questions.question: What distinguishes a stable sorting algorithm from an unstable one?
options: Stable sort preserves the relative order of equal elements
Stable sort guarantees O(n log n) worst case

questions.question: What is the time complexity of inserting into a min-heap of size n?
Which algorithm finds the Minimum Spanning Tree of a graph greedily by always adding the globally cheapest edge that doesn't form a cycle?
What is the space complexity of Depth First Search (DFS) on a graph with V vertices and E edges?
Which of the following problems is solved optimally by a greedy algorithm?
What is an AVL tree?
options: A tree where all leaves are at the same depth
A self-balancing BST where the height difference between left and right subtrees is at most 1
A binary tree where every node has exactly two children

questions.question: What is the time complexity of building a heap from an unsorted array of n elements?
In the context of graph algorithms, what is a 'relaxation' step?
options: Removing an edge from the graph
Updating the shortest known distance to a vertex if a shorter path is found
Marking a vertex as fully processed

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of searching in a hash table with chaining?
Which data structure is most appropriate for implementing a LRU (Least Recently Used) cache?
What does it mean for a problem to have 'optimal substructure'?
options: The problem can be solved in polynomial time
An optimal solution can be constructed from optimal solutions to its subproblems
The problem has multiple valid solutions
The greedy choice always leads to a global optimum

questions.question: What is the time complexity of Bellman-Ford algorithm on a graph with V vertices and E edges?
What is a circular linked list?
options: A linked list whose tail node points back to the head
A doubly linked list with sentinels
A linked list stored in a circular buffer
A linked list that stores only even indices

questions.question: Which of the following sorting algorithms is NOT comparison-based?
What is the 'two-pointer technique' most commonly used for?
options: Traversing a binary tree level by level
Solving problems on sorted arrays or linked lists with O(n) time and O(1) space

questions.question: What is the time complexity of the naive recursive Fibonacci computation fib(n)?
In graph theory, what is a 'strongly connected component' (SCC)?
options: A subgraph where every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree
A maximal subgraph where every vertex is reachable from every other vertex
The largest clique in the graph
A subgraph with no directed cycles

questions.question: What is the sliding window technique primarily used for?
options: Finding the median in a stream of numbers
Efficiently computing aggregates over contiguous subarrays of variable or fixed size
Detecting negative cycles in a graph

questions.question: What is the time complexity of the Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) string matching algorithm for a text of length n and pattern of length m?
What is 'tail recursion' and why does it matter?
options: Recursion where the base case is at the start
A recursive call that is the very last operation in a function, allowing stack-frame reuse
Recursion that always terminates in O(log n) steps

questions.question: What is the key difference between Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms for MST?
options: Prim's works on directed graphs; Kruskal's does not
Prim's grows a single tree from a starting vertex; Kruskal's merges multiple trees by adding cheapest edges globally
Kruskal's requires a priority queue; Prim's does not
They produce different MSTs on the same graph

questions.question: What is the time complexity of the 0/1 Knapsack DP algorithm for n items and capacity W?
Which condition must be true for Binary Search to work correctly?
options: The array must contain distinct elements
The array must have an odd number of elements
The array must be stored as a linked list

questions.question: What is the difference between a tree's 'depth' and its 'height'?
options: Depth and height are the same property
Depth is the number of edges from the root to a node; height is the number of edges from a node to its deepest leaf
Height is measured from the root; depth is always zero for the root
Depth counts nodes; height counts edges
